_about: Regression evals for oak-accessibility. 'trigger_evals' test that the skill description fires for the right queries and not for near-misses (judge sees the full installed skill list and routes each query). 'quality_evals' are graded with assertions, comparing a with-skill run against a no-skill baseline. Re-run when the skill or the base model changes.

trigger_evals.query: Is this slide deck WCAG 2.2 AA? Audit it and tell me what to fix.
Make this slide deck accessible before I share it with my team — nothing to do with Oak.
trigger_evals.note: brand-independence: accessibility is a universal floor; must fire with no Oak/brand mention

trigger_evals.query: Make this Google Doc accessible before we publish it.
Add alt text and fix the heading structure on this report.
Our quiz shows correct answers in green and wrong ones in red — is that an accessibility problem?
What captions and transcript do we need for this lesson video?
Are the tap targets and colour contrast on this web page good enough for accessibility?
What are Oak's brand colours and fonts for this booklet?
trigger_evals.note: oak-brand — visual brand, not an accessibility audit

trigger_evals.query: Rewrite this paragraph so it reads like Oak.
How do I scaffold this Year 9 maths lesson so SEND pupils can access the same content?
Build me a starter quiz on photosynthesis.
trigger_evals.note: oak-lesson-builder / make-quiz; accessibility only applies once it exists

quality_evals.prompt: Audit this slide for accessibility and tell me how to fix it. SLIDE: title styled as big bold text (not a real title placeholder); a photo of a cell with no alt text; key term 'mitochondria' shown only as an image of text; body text is light grey (#9AA0A6) on white; a 'required vs optional' diagram that distinguishes the two only by red and green.
assertions: names WCAG 2.2 AA as the standard
flags the missing real slide title / heading structure
flags the photo's missing alt text
flags text-as-image (mitochondria) and asks for real text
flags insufficient contrast of the grey body text (below 4.5:1; notes Oak's 7:1 target)
flags colour-only distinction (red/green) and recommends text/label or shape as well
gives concrete fixes, not just a list of problems

quality_evals.prompt: We're building an interactive multiple-choice quiz for pupils on the web. What do we need to do to make it accessible?
assertions: requires full keyboard operation with a visible focus indicator
requires correct/incorrect feedback not by colour alone (text/icon too)
mentions target size (>=24px) and/or labels and instructions for options
requires captions/transcript if any media is embedded, or notes it if relevant
frames WCAG 2.2 AA as the floor and references checking contrast
distinguishes this technical accessibility from educational/SEND accessibility or stays correctly scoped to WCAG
